Surah An-Naml (The Ant) [Meccan, and its verses are 93, 94 or 95 verses; it was revealed after Surah Ash-Shu'ara']

﴿Ta Sin.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by that. ﴿These﴾ — these verses — ﴿are the verses of the Qur'an﴾ — verses from it — ﴿and a Book clear﴾ — manifest, making the truth distinct from falsehood. It is a conjunction (ʿatf) with the addition of an attribute (ṣifah).
Guidance (huda) — a guide from misguidance — and good tidings for the believers, those who affirm it, of Paradise.

ِ﴿Alladhina yuqimuna as-salah﴾ (those who establish the prayer): they perform it in its proper form. ﴿Wa yu'tuna﴾ (and they give) ﴿az-zakah﴾ (the zakat): they give it. ﴿Wa hum bil-akhirati hum yuqinun﴾ (and they are certain of the Hereafter): they know it through reasoning. The pronoun "hum" is repeated because the separation between it and the predicate (khabar) is long.

Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter – We have made their deeds appealing to them, [the ugly deeds], by implanting desire in them, until they see them as good. ﴿So they wander blindly﴾ bewildered in them, because of their ugliness in Our sight.

﴿Those are the ones for whom is the evil of punishment﴾, its worst in the world being killing and captivity. ﴿And in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers﴾, because their destination is the everlasting Fire, which will be upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 6:

﴿And indeed you﴾ is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿are being given the Qur'an﴾ it is being cast upon you with intensity ﴿from the presence﴾ from with ﴿of One Wise, All-Knowing﴾ in that matter.

Mention (O Muhammad) when Moses said to his family, meaning his wife, while traveling from Madyan to Egypt: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire﴾, meaning I saw it from afar, ﴿I will bring you from it news﴾ about the state of the road, for he had lost his way, ﴿or bring you a burning brand﴾, where "shihab" is in the genitive construction with "qabas" for explanation, meaning a flame of fire on the head of a wick or a stick, ﴿that you may warm yourselves﴾. The ta' of "tasta-lun" is replaced by ta' (ṭāʾ) from the ta' of the iftiʿāl form, from "ṣaliya bil-nār" (ṣaliya bil-nār, to be warmed by the fire), with the lām vowelled both with kasra and with fatha: you may warm yourselves against the cold.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 27, verse 8:

﴿So when he came to it, he was called: that﴾ i.e., with [the words] ﴿Blessed is﴾, i.e., God has blessed ﴿whoever is in the fire﴾, i.e., Musa, ﴿and whoever is around it﴾, i.e., the angels, or the reverse. Baraka (to bless) is transitive both directly and with a preposition, and one estimates a word after it denoting a place (i.e., baraka man fi al-makan, "blessed is whoever is in the place"). ﴿And glory be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ is part of what he was called, and its meaning is the glorification of God, exalting Him above any evil.
﴿O Musa, indeed it﴾: i.e., the matter (al-sha'n)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 10:

﴿And throw down your staff﴾ so he threw it down, ﴿and when he saw it moving﴾ shaking, ﴿as if it were a jann﴾ a light, swift serpent, ﴿he turned and fled without looking back﴾ returning. ﴿O Musa, do not fear﴾ from it, ﴿indeed, the messengers do not fear before Me﴾ in My presence, ﴿from a serpent or otherwise﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 11:

﴿Illa﴾ (except) meaning, ﴿whoever wrongs﴾ himself, ﴿then substitutes good﴾ that he does ﴿after evil﴾, i.e., repents, ﴿then indeed I am Forgiving, Merciful﴾ (I accept repentance and forgive him).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 12:

﴿And insert your hand into your pocket﴾ (i.e., put your collar over your shirt), ﴿it will come out﴾ different in color from its brown complexion, ﴿white, without any defect﴾ (i.e., leprosy); it has a ray that dazzles the sight, ﴿as one of nine signs﴾ (i.e., sent with them).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 13:

﴿When Our signs came to them, visible,﴾ shining, clear, ﴿they said, "This is clear magic."﴾ evident, manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 14:

﴿And they denied them﴾ — they did not acknowledge them, ﴿while﴾ their souls had ﴿become certain of them﴾, i.e., they were certain that they were from Allah, ﴿in wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ — out of pride, refusing to believe in what Moses brought. ﴿In wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ refers back to ﴿denied﴾. ﴿So see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿what was the end of the corrupters﴾ — which you know from their destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 15:

﴿And We had certainly given knowledge to Dawud (David) and Sulayman (Solomon), his son.﴾ (knowledge) of judgment between the people and the speech of the birds, and other things besides that. ﴿And they both said:﴾ (in gratitude to Allah) ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has favoured us"﴾ with prophethood and by subjecting the jinn, mankind and the devils (to them).

﴿And Solomon inherited from David﴾ prophethood and knowledge, to the exclusion of David's other children. ﴿And he said, "O people, we have been taught the language of the birds"﴾ i.e., the understanding of their calls. ﴿And we have been given of everything﴾ that prophets and kings are given. ﴿Indeed, this﴾ that has been given ﴿is surely the clear bounty﴾ the evident, manifest favour.

﴿And for Sulayman were gathered his hosts of the jinn, the humans and the birds﴾ were assembled, ﴿on a march for him﴾, ﴿and they were being marshalled﴾, meaning they were being assembled and then driven forward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 18:

﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants﴾ — it is in al-Ta'if or in al-Sham — an ant, small or large. ﴿An ant said﴾ — the queen of the ants, who had seen the army of Sulayman. ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his hosts crush you﴾ — lest they break you — ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ — He made the ants occupy the station of the rational ones in the address, by addressing them as such.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 19:

﴿So he smiled, laughing,﴾ Sulayman began to smile, and ended laughing, ﴿at her words.﴾ He had heard it from three miles away, as the wind carried it to him. So he halted his troops when he came overlooking their valley, until they entered their dwellings. His troops were riders and walkers on this journey. ﴿And he said, "My Lord, enable me﴾ to inspire me ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed﴾ upon me ﴿and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You. And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾ the prophets and the saints.

**﴿And he inspected the birds﴾**, to see the hoopoe (al-Hudhud), which can see water under the ground and points to it by pecking into it, so that the devils extract it, because Solomon needed it for the prayer. **﴿But he did not see it﴾**, **﴿so he said: "Why do I not see the hoopoe?"﴾**, meaning: show me what prevented me from seeing it? **﴿Or is it among the absent?﴾** So he did not see it because of its absence. **When he verified it**

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 21:

He said, ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾, by plucking out his feathers and his tail and throwing him into the sun, so that he cannot keep away the insects. ﴿Or I will surely slaughter him﴾, by cutting his throat. ﴿Or he must bring me a clear authority﴾ — with the letter nun doubled and either kasra or fatha, followed by a kasra nun — ﴿a manifest proof﴾, a clear evident proof for his excuse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 22:

﴿Then he stayed not long﴾ (fa-makatha, with the kaf read with a damma and with a fatha), meaning for a short period of time. He came before Sulayman humbly, raising his head and lowering his tail and wings, so [Sulayman] pardoned him and asked him about what had happened to him during his absence. ﴿He said: "I have comprehended that which you have not comprehended"﴾, i.e., I have come to know what you have not come to know. ﴿And I have brought you certain news from Saba'﴾ (read with tanwin and without it, being the name of a tribe in Yemen, named after an ancestor of theirs; with tanwin when considered as a male name, and without tanwin when considered as a tribe or place), ﴿[with] news﴾ (khabar, information).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 23:

﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them﴾, i.e., she is a queen over them, whose name is Bilqis. ﴿And she has been given of all things﴾ that kings need of equipment and provisions. ﴿And she has a great throne﴾, a couch, ﴿its length eighty cubits, its width forty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, made of gold and silver, inlaid with pearls, red rubies, chrysolite, and emeralds, and its legs are of red rubies, chrysolite, and emeralds, upon it seven doors, on each chamber a door, closed.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 27, verse 24:

﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. Satan has made their deeds appear fair to them and has barred them from the path﴾ the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 25:

﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah﴾ i.e., that they should prostrate to Him. The "lā" is inserted (zāʾida), and the "nūn" of "an" is assimilated into it, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾. The clause is in the place of the object of "yahtadūna" (they are guided), with "ilā" omitted. ﴿Who brings forth what is hidden (al-khabʾ)﴾ — a verbal noun in the sense of "that which is hidden" — from the rain and the plants ﴿in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal﴾ in your hearts ﴿and what you disclose﴾ with your tongues.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 27, verse 26:

﴿Allah—there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾ It is a resumptive (istinaf) clause of praise, comprising the Throne of the Most Merciful, in contrast to the throne of Bilqis, and between them there is a great disparity.

Sulayman said to the hoopoe: "We shall see whether you have told the truth or whether you are of the liars" (﴿سَنَنْظُرُ أصَدَقْت أمْ كُنْت مِن الكاذِبِينَ﴾). That is, of this kind [of liars]; this is more emphatic than "or have you lied in it." Then he (the hoopoe) guided them to the water, and they extracted it, drank, performed ablution, and prayed. Then Sulayman wrote a letter, its text being: "From the servant of Allah, Sulayman son of Dawud, to Bilqis, queen of Saba': In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission." Then he sealed it with musk, stamped it with his signet ring, and then said to the hoopoe:

"Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them (ﷺ)..." — no, correcting myself: the honorific is only for the Prophet, so I will not add it here.

Here is the translation:

"Go with this letter of mine and throw it to them." That is, to Bilqis and her people. "Then withdraw from them" – turn away, "and stay close by" – he stood near them, "and see what they will return" – what answer they will send back. So he took it, came to her, and her army was around her, and he threw it into her lap. When she saw it she trembled and submitted out of fear, then she read what was in it.

Then she said to the notables of her people: ﴿O chiefs, indeed I﴾ (with both hamzas pronounced in full, *taḥqīq al-hamzatayn*, and the second hamza eased, *taslīl al-thāniya*, by changing it into a waw with a kasra), ﴿have been delivered a noble letter﴾ (*karīm*, meaning sealed).
﴿Indeed it is from Sulayman, and indeed it is﴾: i.e., its content.

﴿She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair; I would not decide a matter until you are present."﴾

The commentator notes the reading of the verb أفْتُونِي (*afatūnī*, "advise me"). The two hamzas are pronounced fully, which is *taḥqīq* (full realization of the hamza), and the second hamza is eased by changing it into a waw, which is *tashīl* (easing of the hamza). Its meaning is: "Give me your opinion" (أشِيرُوا عَلَيَّ, *ashīrū ʿalayya*). ﴿In my affair﴾ means in my matter. ﴿I would not decide a matter﴾ (قاطِعَة أمْرًا, *qāṭiʿa amran*) means I would not settle or conclude it, ﴿until you are present﴾ (تَشْهَدُونَ, *tashhadūna*) means until you attend, i.e., are present with me.

They said, "We are people of strength and people of severe might, but the decision is yours, so see what you will command."

(Tafsir al-Jalalayn) Meaning: people of strength in war. "And the command is yours, so see what you will command": tell us, and we will obey you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 34:

﴿She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town, they ruin it﴾ by destruction, ﴿and make the most honored of its people the most humiliated." And thus do they act﴾. That is, the senders of the letter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 35:

﴿And indeed, I am sending them a gift, and I will wait to see with what the messengers return﴾, from accepting the gift or rejecting it. If he is a king, he will accept it; if he is a prophet, he will not accept it. So she sent male and female servants, a thousand of each in equal number, and five hundred bricks of gold, and a crown studded with jewels, and musk and ambergris, and other things, along with a messenger carrying a letter. The hoopoe hastened to Sulayman and informed him of the news. So he commanded that bricks of gold and silver be struck, and that a open ground be spread out from his place to a distance of nine farsakhs, and that they build around it a wall overlooking it made of gold and silver, and that the finest beasts of land and sea be brought, together with the sons of the jinn, to the right and left of the open ground.

When the envoy came to Sulayman with the gift, and with him his followers, [Sulayman] said: ﴿Will you aid me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you﴾ of the world. ﴿Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift﴾ out of your pride in the adornments of the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 37:

﴿Return to them﴾ with the gift you brought. ﴿We will surely come to them with hosts that they cannot withstand﴾ (lā qibal), i.e., they have no power to resist them. ﴿And We will surely expel them from there, humbled, and they will be abased﴾ from the land of Saba'. It was named after the name of the father of their tribe. ﴿Humbled and abased﴾ if they do not come to me in submission.

When the messenger returned to her with the gift, she (Bilqis) placed her throne inside seven gates, within her palace, and her palace was within seven palaces. She locked the gates and set guards over them. She then prepared herself to set out to Sulayman, to see what he would command her. She set out with twelve thousand qayl (chieftains), with each qayl accompanied by many thousands. She kept traveling until she drew near to him, within a farsakh (a distance of about three miles), and he perceived her presence.

He said: "O chiefs, which of you [*ayyukum*] will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" Regarding the two hamzas (glottal stops) in *ayyukum*, the same applies as stated earlier. "In submission" means submitting and obedient. So I have the right to take it before that, not after it.

ﷺ is not present here, so no honorific needed. Translating the passage:

﴿He said, "An ifrit (a mighty one) of the jinn"﴾ — he is the strong, the mighty — ﴿"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place"﴾ — where you sit for judgment, and that is from the morning until midday — ﴿"And indeed I am strong for it"﴾ — meaning, for carrying it — ﴿"trustworthy"﴾ — concerning what is in it of jewels and other things. Sulayman said, "I want faster than that."

He who had knowledge of the Book (the revealed Scripture) said, and he was Asif ibn Barkhiya. He was a ṣiddīq (a man of great truthfulness), and he knew the Greatest Name of God (al-Ism al-A'ẓam), such that whenever he called upon Him by it, He answered. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ That is, whenever you look at something with it. He said to him, "Look at the sky," so he looked at it. Then he returned his glance and found it (the throne) placed before him. While he was looking at the sky, Asif called upon God by the Greatest Name to bring it to him, and it came about by its passing beneath the earth until it emerged beneath the throne of Sulayman (Solomon). ﴿So when he saw it settled﴾ at rest, still, ﴿beside him, he said: "This is﴾ that is, its arrival to me, ﴿by the grace of my Lord, to test me﴾ to try me, ﴿whether I will be grateful﴾ — read with the two hamzahs made clear (taḥqīq), or the second changed to an alif, or made easy (tas-hīl) with an alif inserted between the two, or without that insertion — ﴿or ungrateful?﴾ for the blessing. ﴿And whoever is grateful, he is only grateful for his own self﴾ that is, for its sake, because the reward of his gratitude returns to him. ﴿And whoever is ungrateful﴾ for the blessing, ﴿then indeed my Lord is Self-Sufficient﴾ independent of his gratitude, ﴿Generous﴾ in bounty toward those who are ungrateful for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 41:

﴿He said: "Disguise her throne for her, let us see whether she will be guided or whether she will be among those who are not guided."﴾ That is: alter it to a state in which she will not recognize it when she sees it. ﴿Let us see whether she will be guided﴾ to recognizing it, ﴿or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾ to recognizing what has been altered for them. He intended by this to test her intelligence, since it was said that there was something in it; so they altered it, by adding or subtracting something, or otherwise.

When she came, it was said to her: ﴿Is your throne like this?﴾ That is, "Is your throne like this (or 'Is it like this'?)" She said: ﴿It is as if it were it﴾, so she recognised it, and she made it ambiguous to them just as they had made it ambiguous to her, since he did not say, "Is this your throne?" For had it been said, "This is it," she would have said, "Yes." Sulaiman said, when he saw her knowledge and understanding.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 43:

﴿And it had hindered her﴾ from worshipping Allah ﴿from what she used to worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 44:

﴿It was said to her﴾ also, ﴿"Enter the palace (al-sarh)."﴾ It was a surface of clear, white glass beneath which was flowing sweet water with fish in it, which Sulayman (Solomon) had constructed when he was told that her shins and feet were like the feet of a donkey. ﴿So when she saw it, she supposed it was a pool﴾ of water, ﴿and she uncovered her shins﴾ in order to wade through it. Sulayman was on his throne at the front of the palace, and he saw her shins and feet, which were beautiful. ﴿He said﴾ to her, ﴿"Indeed, it is a palace smoothed (mumarrad)﴾ [made smooth] ﴿of glass (qawarir)﴾ [of crystal], and he invited her to Islam. ﴿She said, "My Lord, I have wronged myself"﴾ by worshipping other than You, ﴿"and I submit (aslamtu)"﴾ [being] ﴿"with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ He had intended to marry her, but he disliked the hair on her shins, so the devils prepared a depilatory (nurah) for him, and he removed the hair with it. He then married her, loved her, and confirmed her in her kingdom. He used to visit her once every month and stay with her for three days. Her kingdom ended with the ending of Sulayman's kingdom. It is narrated that he was given the kingdom when he was thirteen years old and died when he was fifty-three years old. So glory be to Him to whom the end of His dominion does not come.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 45:

﴿And We certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih﴾ from their own tribe, ﴿[saying], "Worship Allah"﴾ i.e., that worship Allah, make Him one (waḥḥidūhu), ﴿and then they became two factions contending⟩ over the religion: a faction of believers from the time of his being sent to them, and a faction of disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 46:

﴿He said﴾ to the deniers: "O my people, why do you seek to hasten the evil before the good?" That is, why do you seek the punishment before the mercy, when you say: "If what you have brought us is true, then bring us the punishment." ﴿Why not﴾ (hallā, i.e. "why do you not") ﴿seek forgiveness from Allah﴾ for the shirk (association of partners with Allah), ﴿so that you may be shown mercy﴾, and thus not be punished.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 47:

﴿They said: "We have taken omen from you and from those with you."﴾ Its origin is tatayyarnā (تَطَيَّرْنا), the ta' was assimilated into the ta' (ṭā')... [see note below]

Translation:

﴿They said, "We have taken an omen (ittayyarnā) from you and from those who are with you."﴾ Its origin is taṭayyarnā (تَطَيَّرْنا), the tā' being assimilated into the ṭā' (idghām) and a hamzat al-waṣl (hamzat al-waṣl, the connecting hamza) being brought in. That is: "We have considered you a bad omen (tashā'um) from us," ﴿with you and with those who are with you﴾ — the believers — since they had suffered drought, the rain had stopped and they had gone hungry.

﴿He said, "Your omen is with Allah"﴾ — your ill omen (shu'mukum) — ﴿with Allah﴾; He has brought it to you. ﴿Rather, you are a people being tested﴾ — you are being examined by good and evil.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 48:

﴿And there were in the city﴾ the city of Thamud ﴿nine men﴾ i.e., men ﴿who spread corruption in the land﴾ through acts of disobedience, among them clipping dinars and dirhams ﴿and did not amend﴾ through obedience.

**﴿They said﴾**, meaning some of them said to others: **﴿Swear to one another by God﴾**, meaning take oaths: **﴿"We will surely attack him﴾** with the nun and the ta' (**بِالنُّونِ والتّاء**), with the second ta' given a damma (**وضَمّ التّاء الثّانِيَة**), **﴿and his family﴾**, meaning those who believed in him, **meaning we will kill them by night. ﴿Then we will surely say to his heir﴾** with the nun and the ta' (**بِالنُّونِ والتّاء**), with the second lam given a damma (**وضَمّ اللّام الثّانِيَة**), **﴿to the heir of his blood﴾**, **﴿"We did not witness﴾**, meaning we were not present, **﴿the destruction of his family﴾** with a damma or a fatha on the mim (**بِضَمِّ المِيم وفَتْحها**), meaning their destruction or their perishing, **so we do not know who killed them."**
﴿And they schemed⦆ in that matter ﴿a scheme, and We schemed a scheme⦆, i.e., We requited them by hastening their punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 51:

﴿So look, how was the outcome of their plotting: that We destroyed them﴾ — i.e., We annihilated them — ﴿and their people, all of them.﴾ — by the Cry of Jibril (Jibril), or by the angels pelting them with stones which they could see but which could not see them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 52:

﴿So those are their houses, empty﴾ i.e., vacant (khāliyah). It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), and the element governing it is the meaning of the demonstrative "those" (ishārah). ﴿Because of what they did wrongly﴾ i.e., because of their wrongdoing, namely their disbelief (kufr). ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾ a lesson (ʿibrah) ﴿for a people who know﴾ Our power, so that they take heed (fa-yattaʿiẓūn).
And We saved those who believed, with Salih, and they were four thousand, and they used to fear God, [abstaining from] shirk (associating partners with God).

﴿Lut﴾ is in the accusative (*manṣūb*, "المَنصُوب"), governed by an implied verb placed before it, "اذْكُرْ" (*udhkur*, "remember"). It is also a *badal* (substitution, "بَدَل") for that same term. ﴿When he said to his people, "Do you commit the abomination?"﴾ That is, *al-liwat* (sodomy). ﴿While you see﴾ means that some of you see one another, persisting openly in the disobedience.

﴿أإنَّكُمْ﴾ (with the two hamzas pronounced in full, *tahqiq* [full articulation of the hamza], and the second softened, *tashil* [easing of the hamza], with an alif inserted between them, in both readings) ﴿لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجال شَهْوَة مِن دُون النِّساء بَلْ أنْتُمْ قَوْم تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ (Do you indeed come to males out of lust, instead of women? Rather, you are a people who are ignorant) of the consequence of your deed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 56:

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lut from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ His family ﴿from your town﴾, ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ from the anuses of men.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 57:

﴿So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We had decreed her to be among those who remained behind﴾ — We made her, by Our decree, ﴿among those who remained behind﴾, i.e., those left behind to (suffer) the punishment.
﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ It was stones of sijjil, and it destroyed them. ﴿Evil was﴾ the rain of ﴿those who were warned﴾ with the punishment, their rain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 59:

[Qul] (Say), O Muhammad, [al-hamdu lillah] (all praise is due to Allah) for the destruction of the disbelievers from the earlier nations, [wa salamun 'ala 'ibadihi alladhina istafa] (and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen). [Ah-Allah] (Is it Allah) — here they are the two hamzas, with the second changed to an alif, or eased, or with an alif inserted between the eased and the other one, or left out — [khayrun] (better) for the one who worships Him, [amma yushrikun] (or what they associate). It is read with the ta' (you, plural) and the ya' (they). That is, the people of Makkah associate with Him the gods; [khayrun] (they are better) for their worshippers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 60:

﴿Is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, so We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight⁠—﴾ Here there is an iltifat (shift) from the third person (ghaybah) to the first person (takallum). ﴿Gardens⁠﴾ is the plural of ḥadīqah, which is an enclosed orchard. ﴿Of delight⁠﴾ means beauty. ﴿You could not have caused their trees to grow.⁠﴾ Because you lack the power to do so. ﴿Is there any god with Allah?⁠﴾ Read with the two hamzahs pronounced, or with the second softened and an alif inserted between them, in both readings, in its seven places. ﴿With Allah?⁠﴾ Has helped them in that. That is, there is no god with Him. ﴿Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals⁠﴾ to Allah, associating others with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 61:

﴿Is He who made the earth a stable abode﴾ not shaking with its inhabitants, ﴿and made rivers within it﴾ between its parts, ﴿and made for it firmly set mountains﴾ mountains by which He made the earth firm, ﴿and made between the two seas a barrier﴾ between the sweet and the salt, so that neither of them mixes with the other, ﴿is there another god with Allah? Nay, but most of them do not know﴾ His oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 62:

﴿Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil,﴾ the distressed one, the afflicted one whom harm has touched, ﴿when he calls upon Him,﴾ and removes the evil from him and from others, ﴿and makes you successors (khulafa') of the earth?﴾ The idafa (construction) here carries the meaning of "in," i.e., He makes each generation succeed the generation before it. ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember,﴾ little do you take heed, read with the ta' in the second person (tatadhakkarun) and with the ya' in the third person (yatadhakkarun). In it there is idgham (assimilation) of the ta' into the dhal, and ma is extra, serving to diminish the little.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 63:

﴿Or who guides you﴾ (amman yahdikum) guides you to your destinations, ﴿in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾ by the stars at night and by the landmarks of the earth by day, ﴿and who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy﴾ before the rain. ﴿Is there any god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ other than Him.

﴿Is He who originates creation﴾ in the wombs from a drop of semen, ﴿then repeats it﴾ after death, even though you do not acknowledge the repetition, because the proofs for it are established, ﴿and who provides for you from the heaven﴾, providing you with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾, providing you with plants? ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ That is, none does any of what has been mentioned except Allah, and there is no god with Him. ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿Bring your proof﴾, your argument, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that there is with me a god who has done any of what has been mentioned. They asked him about the time of the Hour, so it was revealed

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 65:

﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen, except Allah.﴾ [They are] from the angels and humankind. ﴿The unseen﴾ i.e., what is hidden from them. ﴿Except﴾ but ﴿Allah﴾ knows it. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and others like them, ﴿when﴾ the time [of their resurrection will be].

﴿Bal﴾ [means] ﴿hal﴾ (هَلْ, "whether"). ﴿Idda'āraka﴾ (ادّارَكَ) is in the pattern of ﴿akrama﴾ (أكْرَمَ, "to honor"). In another reading it is ﴿ad-darraka﴾ (ادّارَكَ) with the ﴿d﴾ (الدّال) doubled. Its origin is ﴿tadāraka﴾ (تَدارَكَ), in which the ﴿t﴾ (التّاء) was changed into a ﴿d﴾ through substitution (ibdāl) and then assimilated into the following ﴿d﴾ through assimilation (idghām), and the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in. It means: it reached, caught up, or followed one another and came in succession. ﴿Their knowledge of the Hereafter﴾, meaning, concerning it, to the point that they asked about the time of its coming. ﴿The matter is not so.﴾ ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾ ﴿Blind﴾ is from blindness of the heart, and it is more emphatic than what precedes it. The original form is ﴿ʿamayūna﴾ (عَمَيُونَ), but the ﴿ḍamma﴾ (الضَّمَّة, the vowel "u") was felt to be heavy on the ﴿y﴾ (الياء), so it was moved to the ﴿m﴾ (الميم) after the removal of its ﴿kasra﴾ (الكَسْرَة, the vowel "i").
"And those who disbelieved said," also, denying the Resurrection, "When we and our fathers have become dust, shall we indeed be brought forth [from the graves]?"

Commentary of al-Maḥallī and al-Suyūṭī (Tafsīr al-Jalālayn) on Sūrah 27, verse 68:

﴿We have been promised this, we and our fathers before, if﴾ "what" ﴿this is not but the tales of the ancients﴾. "Tales" is the plural of ﴿أُسْطُورَة﴾ (ustūrah), with a ḍamma (بِالضَّمِّ) on the first letter, meaning what has been written down of falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 69:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see how was the end of the criminals."﴾ By their denial, and it was their destruction by punishment.

﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot.﴾ This is consolation (tasliyah, comfort given to one who is distressed) for the Prophet (ﷺ). That is: do not concern yourself with their plotting against you, for We will be your helper against them.
﴿And they say, "When is this promise [of punishment],"﴾ [i.e., this threat of punishment] ﴿"if you are truthful?"﴾ [in it].

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 27, verse 72:

﴿Say: "It may be that some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you."﴾ (radifa means) drew near (qaraba) ﴿to you﴾. So there befell them the killing at Badr, and the rest of the punishment comes to them after death.

And indeed your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind (﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind﴾), and among it is the postponement of punishment for the disbelievers (﴿but most of them do not give thanks﴾). So the disbelievers do not give thanks for the postponement of punishment, because they deny its occurrence.
And indeed your Lord knows what their breasts conceal (﻿tukhfīhi, i.e., what they hide) and what they declare with their tongues.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 75:

﴿And there is not a thing hidden in the heaven or the earth﴾ The ha' (in ghaaʾiba) is for emphasis (mubalagha): any thing that is in the utmost degree of concealment from people, ﴿except that it is in a clear Record﴾ manifest, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and the hidden knowledge of Him, exalted is He, and among it is the punishment of the disbelievers.

Indeed, this Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel (those present in the time of our Prophet) most of that about which they differ, (namely) by clarifying what has been mentioned in its correct manner, which would settle their disagreement among them, had they adhered to it and submitted.
[And indeed it is] ﴿guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and mercy for the believers﴾ from punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 78:

﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, as He will judge others, ﴿by His judgment﴾, i.e., His justice, ﴿and He is the Mighty﴾, the Overpowering, ﴿the Knowing﴾ of what He judges, so He does not allow anyone to oppose Him, as the disbelievers opposed His prophets in the worldly life.

Surah 27, verse 79 — Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti):

﴿So put your trust in God﴾ (thiq bihi) — rely on Him, ﴿indeed you are upon the manifest truth﴾ (al-din al-bayyin), the clear religion. So the final outcome is yours, with victory over the disbelievers. Then He set forth parables for them, likening them to the dead, the deaf, and the blind.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti on surah 27, verse 80:

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when﴾ with the pronunciation of the two hamzas in full (tahqiq, "making clear") and the softening of the second hamza (tashil, "easing"), so that it is pronounced between hamza and the letter ya.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 81:

﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, the Qur'an, and so they are Muslims﴾ — sincerely devoted (mukhlisun) to the Oneness of Allah.

﴿When the word has come into effect against them﴾, meaning the punishment has become due to befall them along with the disbelievers, ﴿We shall bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them﴾, i.e., it will speak to those present at the time of its emergence, in Arabic, telling them among the things it says: ﴿that the people﴾ (the disbelievers of Makkah) ﴿were not certain of Our signs﴾, i.e., they did not believe in the Qur'an, which includes the resurrection (al-ba'th), the reckoning (al-hisab), and the punishment (al-'iqab). With its emergence, the enjoining of good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf) and the forbidding of evil (al-nahy 'an al-munkar) will cease, and no disbeliever will believe, just as God revealed to Nuh (Noah). ﴿Indeed, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾.

On the reading with the hamzah of ﴿إنّ﴾ pronounced with a fatha (i.e., "anna"), the particle "bi" (with) is to be understood as supplied after "tukallimuhum" (it speaks to them), so that the sense is "it speaks to them with [the statement] that the people..."

And mention the Day when We shall gather from every nation a crowd (jama'ah) of those who denied Our signs, and they will be driven in ranks, meaning they will be assembled by holding back the last of them until the first of them catches up, and then they will be driven on.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 84:

﴿Until, when they have come,﴾ to the place of reckoning, ﴿He will say﴾ (exalted is He) to them: ﴿"Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge? Or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ That is, "Did you deny My prophets concerning My signs, while you had not encompassed, from the aspect of your denial of them, any knowledge of them? Or what was it that you were doing, of what you were commanded?" In ﴿أمّا﴾ (amma) there is idgham (assimilation, i.e., the merging of two identical consonants) of ما (ma), the interrogative particle, and ﴿ذا﴾ (dha) is a relative pronoun (mawsul), meaning ما الَّذِي (ma alladhi, "what it is that").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 85:

﴿And the word will come to pass﴾ — the punishment is due — ﴿against them because they wronged﴾ — i.e., they associated partners [with Allah] — ﴿and they will not be able to speak﴾ — since they will have no argument.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 86:

﴿Have they not seen that We made the night﴾ (We created) ﴿for them to rest therein﴾ (like the rest of mankind) ﴿and the day to see by﴾ (meaning, in which one sees) ﴿so that they may go about their affairs therein.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ (proofs) ﴿of His power, Exalted is He,﴾ ﴿for a people who believe.﴾ (They are singled out for mention because they benefit from them in faith, unlike the disbelievers.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 87:

﴿And the day the Horn is blown﴾ — al-Qarn (the Horn), the first blast, from Israfil (Israfil). ﴿Then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾ — they will fear with the fear that leads to death, as in another verse, ﴿and so will fall unconscious﴾; and the expression here is in the past tense to indicate the certainty of its occurrence. ﴿Except whom Allah wills﴾ — that is, Jibril (Jibril), Mika'il (Mika'il), Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that they are the martyrs, for they are alive with their Lord, being provided for. ﴿And all﴾ — its tanwin is a substitute for the omitted genitive noun, meaning: and all of them, after their revival, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will come to Him﴾ — in the form of the verb and the active participle — ﴿humbled﴾, meaning abased. And the expression of their coming in the past tense is to indicate the certainty of its occurrence.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 88:

﴿And you see the mountains﴾ you watch them at the time of the blast (al-nafkha) ﴿you think them﴾ you suppose them ﴿motionless﴾ standing still in their places because of their greatness ﴿while they pass by as the passing of clouds﴾ like the rain when the wind drives it, i.e., they proceed at its pace until they fall upon the earth and become level with it, scattered (mabthuthah); then they become like wool (al-ihn), then they become scattered dust (habaan manthuran) ﴿the handiwork of God﴾ a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the content of the sentence before it, and it is annexed to its agent after its operator has been omitted, i.e., God made that as a making ﴿who perfected﴾ made firm ﴿everything﴾ He made ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾ with the ya' and the ta' (readings), i.e., His enemies from disobedience and His allies from obedience

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 89:

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah," on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿for him there is something better﴾, i.e., reward, ﴿than it﴾, i.e., because of it. [The preposition "than" (min)] is not for comparison, since there is no good deed better than it. In another verse [it says]: ﴿ten times as much﴾ [6:160].

﴿And they﴾, i.e., those who come with it, ﴿from terror that Day﴾ [are secure]. It is read with the genitive construction (idafah) and with kasrah on the mim, and also with fathah on the mim, and "fazaʿ" (terror) read with tanwin and fathah on the mim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 90:

﴿And whoever comes with the evil deed﴾, i.e., shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿their faces will be thrown into the Fire﴾, by being cast into it face-first. The faces are mentioned because they are the seat of honour among the senses, so what is other than them is included a fortiori. It will be said to them as a rebuke: ﴿Are you recompensed except﴾ with the recompense ﴿for what you used to do﴾ of shirk and sins? Say to them...

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 91:

﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city﴾, i.e., Makkah, ﴿who has made it sacred﴾, making it a sanctuary (haram) in which none shed the blood of a human being, none is wronged, its game is not hunted, and its grass is not cut. This is among the favours upon the Quraysh, its people, in that Allah lifted from their land the punishment and the widespread afflictions present in all the lands of the Arabs. ﴿And to Him belongs everything﴾, so He is its Lord, its Creator, and its Owner. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, submitting to Allah by His Oneness.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary on Surah 27 (al-Naml), verse 92:

﴿And that I should recite the Qur'an﴾ to you, namely, the recitation of the call to faith. ﴿Whoever is guided﴾ by it ﴿is only guided for his own soul﴾, i.e., for its benefit, for the reward of his being guided belongs to him. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ from faith and misses the path of guidance, ﴿say﴾ to him: ﴿I am only one of the warners﴾, those who frighten. There is nothing incumbent upon me but conveyance (of the message), and this was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 27, verse 93:

﴿And say: "All praise is for Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them."﴾ Allah showed them on the Day of Badr the killing and the taking of captives, and the angels struck their faces and their backs, and Allah hastened them to the Fire. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ It is read with the ya' (third person, "they do") and with the ta' (second person, "you do"). And He only gives them respite until their appointed time.
